title: Any gate that reads a component's health as a precondition misfires when that health IS the work — and the answer is a second checkable shape, never an exemption
question: Ticket c691e19d5464 could not cross PROVED. Its job was repairing a RED proof, so at BUILDME the proven-space rung (which accepts only a GREEN proof) was unsatisfiable honestly; the build named an unrelated green proof to open the door, and the coverage rung at PROVED correctly refused it for not covering the ticket. Is this the coverage rung being too strict, a case for an approved exemption, or something else?
ruling: Something else, and Akien named the category. Akien, 2026-09-11, verbatim: 'any gate that reads a component's health as a precondition will misfire whenever that component's health is the work. When that happens, the answer is a second checkable shape, never an exemption. the broken thing gets declared at ticketing to be the subject of the repair, and thus allowed this.'
the_category: WORKING ON MYSELF. Akien, 2026-09-11: 'this issue is part of a category of issues related to working on myself. they are things that would be non-issues working on an external project. one of the issues with you being everybody is this issue of lying to yourself. makes sense. that's why we built hard gates after all.' On an external project the instrument and the subject are different objects; here the instrument IS the subject, and every gate that reads 'green = solid ground to stand on' mis-reads 'red = the thing I am here to fix.'
where_the_defect_actually_is: AT BUILDME, NOT AT PROVED. The coverage rung did its job: it caught a proof named as a warrant that the build was never leaning on. Weakening it (the option CC recommended) would have suppressed the alarm that found the real defect — which is itself the self-deception this category is made of. The proven-space rung at BUILDME accepts exactly one shape of answer to 'is the ground solid?', and for a repair ticket the honest answer is 'no, and that is why I am here.'
the_second_shape: The ticket DECLARES, AT TICKETING (the /sorted cast — before the build, where the claim is a prediction rather than a rationalisation), that a named broken artifact is the SUBJECT of the repair. The proven-space rung then accepts that named RED proof as the crossing's warrant, gated on deterministic checks, no prose: (1) the named proof's standing seal really is RED — a green one has nothing to repair and refuses; (2) that proof already declares this ticket; (3) the artifact is one this ticket declared it would touch. The record then says what actually happened, the only proof the ticket ever names is its own, and THE COVERAGE RUNG AT PROVED PASSES UNCHANGED. Nothing weakens; the start rung goes from one laundered claim to three checkable ones.
why_not_an_exemption: An exemption is prose, and prose does not pass a gate (Akien's standing rule). It would also be the system granting ITSELF permission — and this is the one category where the pressure to plaster is highest, because the gate is blocking its own repair. Akien floated an approved-exemption option ('this is a working on myself issue and akien has approved it thusly') and then ruled against that shape in the same breath by naming the better one.
traces_to: Law 4 (a rule that matters is enforced by physics, not policy — a second shape is physics, an exemption is policy)
Law 8 (prove then trust — the warrant must be what the build actually leaned on, or the trust is bought with a false receipt)
Law 7 (a record of truth may never collapse an error — naming an unrelated green proof made the crossing record false)
Law 9 (red is the default; the red proof is the subject, not an obstacle to route around)
known_members_of_the_category: c691e19d5464 — repairs a red proof; the ticket that surfaced this.
3dfceaa272ec-a-timeout-is-not-a-red — repairs the test runner; B8 on the build queue, and it will hit the same wall.
owed_physics: Built under c691e19d5464 per bounds ruling 2026-09-09-a-bug-the-voyage-uncovers-is-fixed-by-that-voyage. MEASURED 2026-09-11, so the build is execution and not design: (a) THE FIELD is `repairs` on the TICKET — a list of proof paths, read by the gate from owner.ticket and NEVER from the crossing, which is what makes 'declared at ticketing' physics rather than a habit: a builder cannot invent it at crossing time. It is already written on c691e19d5464. /sorted's door gains it as an optional field. (b) THE RUNG is rule 2 in cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master/clearance.py, the loop at lines 1306-1319. A named proof whose seal is not green is accepted IFF: its path is in the ticket's `repairs`; proof_coverage.declared(path) carries an entry for this boat_id; standing(path)['seal'] is NOT None (an UNSEALED proof is not a red proof, it is an unmeasured one — Law 3 — and must still refuse); and the target is not PROVED. (c) THE TERMINAL STAYS HONEST FOR FREE: at PROVED the same rule 2 still demands green, so a declared repair that never happened refuses at the terminal. Rule 2b needs no change at all — by (b)'s second check the only proof the ticket names already declares it. (d) THE GOTCHA: `proven` (line 1306) feeds proven_seal_date onto the crossing record at line 1385, so it must not stay None when every named proof is a repair subject. Take the first GREEN seal if there is one, else the repair subject's red seal, and stamp the repair declaration onto the crossing so the record says which shape cleared it (Law 7 — the record may not read as a green warrant when it was a declared repair). (e) THE TEETH are hermetic, in the clearance proof's fixture world, never against the live corpus.
supersedes_nothing: The coverage rung (rule 2b) is untouched by this ruling, as is its four-of-twelve finding from 2026-09-07.
and_b5_itself: c691e19d5464's BUILDME crossing already stands, naming cairn/tools/cairnmap/proofs/test_cairnmap.py — the false warrant. Fixing the gate does not retroactively fix that record. The honest close is a RETREAT to BUILDME (explicitly legal; the gate refuses only forward motion, and there is precedent in this session's own log at cairn b26ea43) and a re-crossing that names the proof the build actually leaned on and repaired, skills/intent/proofs/test_intent_skill.py — which is GREEN now, so it clears on the FIRST shape. The second shape is therefore proved by fixture teeth, not by B5, which is correct: a gate is proved with fixtures.
